title: MoE-Infinity: Efficient MoE Inference on Personal Machines with Sparsity-Aware Expert Cache (Xue, Fu, Lu, Sun, Mai, Marina; Edinburgh)
setup: batch 1; RTX A5000 24GB, PCIe4 (24 GB/s Table 1, 32 GB/s text); all experts in host DRAM 32GB-1TB, no SSD; DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Mixtral-8x7B, Switch, NLLB, Arctic; prompt 512 decode 32; baselines DeepSpeed-Inference, llama.cpp, Mixtral-Offloading, vLLM, BrainStorm (reimplemented)

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: DeepSeek-V2-Lite avg TPOT vs vLLM..Ollama; conclusion says 2.7-13.7x
LRU cited as baseline; no SSD tier

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: first pass: hardware not on page
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: A5000 24GB, PCIe4, host DRAM 32GB-1TB

why: GPU VRAM cache over host DRAM, GPU-offload baselines, no SSD, 64-128 experts, all weights fit in host RAM; cache is share of VRAM not 2-4 footprints
ablation: EAMC capacity (Fig 9); workload shift (Table 3); no separate cache vs prefetch vs policy ablation
limitations: batch 1 personal use only; multi-server future work; long context shrinks expert buffer (falls to on-demand at 2^17)
contradicts_our_findings: no; states LRU is the common implementation and reuse skew exists only within a request

title: OD-MoE: On-Demand Expert Loading for Cacheless Edge-Distributed MoE Inference (Wang, Du, Pan, Liew, Liu, Chen; CUHK)
setup: Mixtral-8x7B, greedy, batch 1; 10 nodes: main 1x3090, shadow 2x3090 INT8, 8 workers 1x3090 192GB DRAM, R7-7700, 1 GbE; baselines on 8x3090 EPYC 7K62 512GB; 60 Alpaca prompts (16/128 in, 64/256 out); footnote: no SSD/NVMe due to large access delay

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: cacheless parallel loading from worker DRAM
as above

why: GPU nodes, DRAM tier, 8-expert model, shadow predictor needs a second model; authors reject SSD
quality_loss: none for OD-MoE (full precision); baselines lose (MMLU 70.34 vs 49.82-55.26; GSM8K 64.14 vs 22-60)
ablation: yes: alignment (token/KV) and shadow vs random prefetch vs no prefetch (Fig 8-9)
limitations: shadow node GPU memory; network delays
contradicts_our_findings: no; its MoE-Infinity reproduction (0.69 tok/s) is far below P-0211 claims
